title: Delivery management at Witik

summary: Coordinate a 10-person team and releases for a platform serving 20,000+ users.

details.title: Connect business, product and engineering
details.body: I manage the backlog through Azure DevOps and coordinate business, product, QA and development. Tracking risks and priorities is part of this responsibility.

details.title: Support end-to-end delivery
details.body: My scope includes release tracking, deliverable quality and coordination of a team of 6 developers, 2 QA engineers, 1 product owner and me as Tech Lead Delivery.

takeaways: Backlog, risk and release management with Azure DevOps.
Experience with a B2B SaaS platform serving 100+ clients.
evidenceNote: These figures describe platform scale and release cadence. They do not measure an improvement attributable to any single action.

title: AI adoption in code reviews
context: At Witik, the 10-person delivery team (6 developers, 2 QA engineers, 1 product owner and me as Tech Lead Delivery) contributes to a B2B SaaS platform used by 20,000+ users and 100+ clients.
action: I introduced Claude Code for assisted reviews, structured prompts and automated quality checklists.
result: Three practices are now structured in the team workflow: assisted reviews, shared prompts and quality checklists. No reliable before/after figures are available to quantify their effect on lead time or defect rates.
summary: Establish three shared practices: assisted reviews, prompts and quality checklists.

details.title: Start with engineering practices
details.body: I introduced Claude Code for assisted reviews, structured prompts and automated quality checklists. Team needs guide use of the tool.

details.title: Keep human judgment
details.body: AI assists the work; the team remains responsible for technical decisions and deliverables. The manager supports adoption and preserves quality.

takeaways: AI adoption within the team workflow.
Technical responsibility retained by the team.
evidenceNote: The three practices are part of the workflow. No reliable before-and-after measurements are available to quantify their effect on lead time or defect rates.
